empty: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Denote by $\emptyset$ the initial presheaf on $\mathcal{C}$ and by $\emptyset^\#$ its associated sheaf, the initial object of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})$. An object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ is called sheaf-theoretically empty when $\emptyset^\#\to h_U^\#$ is an isomorphism.
almost: Let $\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}$ be sites. A functor $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ is almost cocontinuous when, for every $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C})$ and each covering $\{V_j\to u(U)\}_{j\in J}$ of $\mathcal{D}$, there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ of $\mathcal{C}$ such that for each $i$, either $u(U_i)$ is sheaf-theoretically empty or $u(U_i)\to u(U)$ factors through some $V_j\to u(U)$. Here sheaf-theoretically empty means $\emptyset^\#\to h_{u(U_i)}^\#$ is an isomorphism of sheaves on $\mathcal{D}$. The presheaf functor $u^p$ is precomposition with $u$, and for continuous $u$ its restriction $u^s$ sends sheaves to sheaves.
subtopos: A morphism of topoi $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})$ is an embedding when $f_*$ is fully faithful. A subtopos of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})$ is a strictly full subcategory which is the essential image of such a fully faithful direct-image functor. A closed subtopos can be described from a subterminal sheaf $\mathcal{F}\hookrightarrow *$ as the full subcategory of sheaves $\mathcal{G}$ for which $\mathcal{F}\times\mathcal{G}\to\mathcal{F}$ is an isomorphism. A closed immersion is a topos embedding with closed essential image.
algebra: For a continuous functor $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ of sites, the sufficient conditions from the earlier site-morphism criterion are: $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ for which $u(X)$ is final in $\mathcal{D}$, and $\mathcal{C}$ has fibre products preserved by $u$. Under these assumptions $u$ determines a morphism of sites $f:\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}$ with pullback $f^{-1}=u_s$ and pushforward $f_*=u^s$. For the corresponding presheaf functors $u_p\dashv u^p$, write $u_p$ for the colimit-defined left extension and $u^p$ for precomposition.
topology: For a category $\mathcal{C}$ and $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C})$, a sieve $S$ on $U$ is a subpresheaf $S\subset h_U$, equivalently a collection of arrows into $U$ closed under precomposition. The sieve generated by an arrow family $\{U_i\to U\}$ is the smallest such subpresheaf containing all its members. A Grothendieck topology $J$ assigns to each $U$ a set $J(U)$ of covering sieves, containing $h_U$, stable under pullback, and satisfying local character: if $S\in J(U)$ and $S'\times_U V$ covers every arrow $V\to U$ in $S$, then $S'\in J(U)$. A presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ is a sheaf for $J$ when $\mathcal{F}(U)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(S,\mathcal{F})$ is bijective for every $U$ and $S\in J(U)$. For an ordinary site its sheaf condition is matching-and-gluing over all source covering families.
L: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category with a Grothendieck topology $J$. For each presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ define $L\mathcal{F}(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{S\in J(U)^{opp}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(S,\mathcal{F})$ where the covering sieves $S$ are ordered by inclusion and restrictions use pullbacks of covering sieves along arrows $V\to U$. The inclusion of the maximal sieve $h_U$ determines $\ell:\mathcal{F}\to L\mathcal{F}$. The resulting sheafification is $\mathcal{F}^\#=L(L\mathcal{F})$ with its canonical map from $\mathcal{F}$.
